claim: On February 6, 2026, NAT gateway discounts were extended to NAT gateways service-chained with secondary firewall endpoints, and the extra Advanced Inspection data processing charge, which ranged from $0.001/GB to $0.009/GB in 13 Regions, was removed.
question: What changed in Network Firewall pricing in February 2026?

values.spoken: a tenth of a cent to almost a cent per gigabyte

qualifiers.scope: all Regions where Network Firewall is offered

evidence.quote: With these improvements, the NAT Gateway discounts now apply when service-chained with both primary and secondary firewall endpoints.

Customers also no longer pay the additional data processing charge for Advanced Inspection that ranged from $0.001/GB to $0.009/GB in 13 AWS regions: Middle East (Bahrain), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), EU (Milan), South America (São Paulo), US West (N. California), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Melbourne).
Posted on: Feb 6, 2026
evidence.heading: AWS Network Firewall announces new price reductions

claim: On May 28, 2025, Network Firewall added VPC endpoint associations, which deploy one firewall across multiple VPCs and allow multiple firewall endpoints in one Availability Zone, with a fixed quota of 50 per firewall per Availability Zone.
question: When did Network Firewall add VPC endpoint associations, and what is their limit?

evidence.quote: | [New type of firewall endpoint for extending firewall capabilities](firewalls.md) | VPC endpoint associations let you deploy a firewall across multiple VPCs and provision multiple firewall endpoints in a single Availability Zone. | May 28, 2025 |

| [Added service quotas for VPC endpoint associations](quotas.md) | VPC endpoints associations have a fixed quota of 50 VPC endpoint associations allowed per firewall, per Availability Zone. VPC endpoints also have an adjustable quota of 300 VPC endpoint associations are allowed per account, per Region. | May 28, 2025 |

note: FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed. Older answers assume one firewall endpoint per AZ in one VPC, or one firewall per VPC.

claim: You can create VPC endpoint associations for any VPC, but only in Availability Zones where the firewall already has a primary endpoint.
question: Where can you create Network Firewall VPC endpoint associations?

values.display: only in Availability Zones where the firewall already has a primary endpoint

evidence.quote: You can create VPC endpoint associations for any VPC, but only in Availability Zones where the firewall already has a primary endpoint defined.

claim: Since June 16, 2025, a Network Firewall firewall can be attached directly to a transit gateway as a transit gateway attachment (a transit gateway-attached firewall), with no extra charge beyond standard Network Firewall and Transit Gateway pricing.
question: Can AWS Network Firewall attach directly to a transit gateway, and since when?

values.display: attach a Network Firewall directly to a transit gateway

evidence.quote: | [Enhanced transit gateway firewall support](tgw-firewall.md) | You can provision firewalls using networking configuration settings shared with your account from AWS Transit Gateway account owners. | June 16, 2025 |
Firewall owners can attach a Network Firewall directly to a transit gateway as a transit gateway attachment either within their own account or shared from a different account.
There are no additional charges for this native integration beyond standard pricing of AWS Network Firewall and AWS Transit Gateway.

note: FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed. The What's New post (June 16, 2025) says the launch covered 5 Regions; no saved page gives today's Region list. Centralized inspection answers no longer need a separate inspection VPC with firewall subnets when this option is available; older questions assume an inspection VPC behind the transit gateway.

claim: Appliance mode is always enabled on transit gateway-attached firewalls, and their traffic is routed through transit gateway route tables, not VPC route tables.
question: How is traffic routed to a transit gateway-attached Network Firewall?

values.display: transit gateway route tables, not VPC route tables

evidence.quote: Appliance mode is always enabled on transit gateway-attached firewalls.
Traffic for transit gateway-attached firewalls must be routed through transit gateway route tables, not VPC route tables.

claim: On August 3, 2026, Network Firewall added a no-source-preservation (proxy) mode in public preview, only in US East (Ohio), in which the firewall acts as an explicit forward proxy behind an attached NAT gateway.
question: What is Network Firewall no-source-preservation mode, and is it generally available?

evidence.quote: | [Network Firewall no-source-preservation (proxy) mode](what-is-aws-network-firewall.md) | AWS Network Firewall now supports the no-source-preservation deployment mode, which allows the firewall to function as an explicit forward proxy that terminates client connections and re-establishes them to destinations using an attached NAT gateway's IP address. This feature is in public preview and is available only in the US East (Ohio) Region (us-east-2). The previously available deployment mode is now referred to as source-preservation mode. For more information, see [No-source-preservation mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/nfw-no-source-preservation.html). | August 3, 2026 |
Network Firewall no-source-preservation mode is in public preview and is available only in the US East (Ohio) Region (us-east-2).

note: NOT EXAMINABLE (preview, after 2026-07-15). Source-preservation mode is the default; the mode cannot be changed after the firewall is created.
